backend.Java / Spring Boot: Clean architecture: domain / application / infrastructure / web. Domain independent of Spring. No business logic in controllers. Validation through Bean Validation, errors through a global handler matching the contract's `Error` schema. JUnit 5 + Mockito tests, integration tests with Spring Boot Test.
backend.Node.js / NestJS: Modules, controllers, services and providers; validated DTOs (class-validator); exception filters matching the `Error` schema. Jest tests. Strict TypeScript.
backend.Node.js / Express: Thin routes, logic in services, input validation (zod or equivalent), error middleware matching the `Error` schema. Jest or Vitest tests.
backend.Python / FastAPI: Pydantic models aligned with the contract, thin routers, dependency injection, exception handlers matching the `Error` schema. pytest tests. Type annotations.
backend.Python / Django: Models and DRF serializers aligned with the contract, thin views, logic in services. Versioned migrations. pytest-django tests.
backend.PHP / Laravel: Thin controllers, FormRequest for validation, API resources aligned with the contract, services for business logic. Migrations. Pest or PHPUnit tests.
backend.PHP / Symfony: Thin controllers, services autowired through the container, DTOs and Validator constraints aligned with the contract, an exception listener matching the `Error` schema. Doctrine migrations. PHPUnit tests.
backend.PHP: Follow the project's structure and PSR-12. Thin entry points, logic in testable classes, prepared statements only, input validated at the boundary, errors matching the `Error` schema. PHPUnit tests.
backend..NET / ASP.NET Core: Thin controllers or minimal endpoints, DTOs aligned with the contract, application services, error middleware matching the `Error` schema. xUnit tests.
backend.Go: Small cohesive packages, consumer-side interfaces, explicit errors, thin handlers. Table-driven tests.

frontend_mobile.React: Function components and hooks, local state first, API calls isolated in a dedicated layer typed from the contract. Testing Library tests. Strict TypeScript.
frontend_mobile.Next.js: App Router or Pages according to what exists (do not mix), deliberate server/client components, server-side data when relevant. Testing Library tests.
frontend_mobile.Angular: Standalone components if the project uses them, services for HTTP calls typed from the contract, controlled RxJS (unsubscribing), reactive forms. Jasmine/Karma or Jest tests according to what exists.
frontend_mobile.Vue / Nuxt: Composition API, composables for shared logic, store (Pinia) only if needed. Vitest + Vue Test Utils tests.
frontend_mobile.SvelteKit: Runes or stores according to the Svelte version in use, server `load` functions for data, API layer typed from the contract. Vitest + Testing Library tests.
frontend_mobile.Astro: Static by default, islands only where interaction requires it, content collections for content, API layer typed from the contract. Vitest tests where there is logic.
frontend_mobile.Flutter: Small widgets, separation of presentation and state, API client generated or typed from the contract, explicit handling of loading and error states. Widget and unit tests.
frontend_mobile.React Native: Function components, navigation according to what exists, API layer typed from the contract, offline states if the spec requires them. Jest + Testing Library tests.
frontend_mobile.Kotlin / Jetpack Compose: Stateless composables when possible, ViewModel + StateFlow for state, Retrofit client typed from the contract, explicit screen states. ViewModel unit tests.
frontend_mobile.Swift / SwiftUI: Light views, state through `@State`/`@Observable` according to the target version, network layer typed from the contract. XCTest tests.

data.PostgreSQL: Versioned migrations, never edit a migration already applied. Explicit constraints and indexes, parameterized queries. Any destructive migration requires explicit consent.
data.MySQL: Versioned migrations, never edit a migration already applied. Beware of locks on ALTER, parameterized queries. Any destructive migration requires explicit consent.
data.MongoDB: Schemas validated in the database or application, indexes justified by queries, idempotent migration scripts. Any data deletion requires explicit consent.
data.Oracle: Versioned migrations (Flyway or Liquibase according to what exists), explicit sequences and constraints, parameterized queries. Any destructive migration requires explicit consent.

devops.Docker: Multi-stage images, non-root user, secrets only through environment variables. Never deploy for real without explicit consent.
devops.GitHub Actions: Actions pinned to a version, minimal permissions, secrets through the repository vault. Never deploy for real without explicit consent.
devops.GitLab CI: Small cached stages, protected variables for secrets. Never deploy for real without explicit consent.
devops.Kubernetes: Declarative manifests, resources and probes set, secrets outside the repository. Apply nothing on a cluster without explicit consent.
devops.Terraform: Small modules, remote state, `plan` only; `apply` and `destroy` require explicit consent.
devops.Docker + GitHub Actions: Multi-stage images and non-root user; pinned actions, minimal permissions, secrets through the repository vault. Never deploy for real without explicit consent.
